sentences.text: BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE DEVNARAYAN MISHRA  ON THE 7 th OF OCTOBER, 2025  MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 33454 of 2025  SUNIL PANIKA @ BANSHU

Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH  Appearance:
 Shri Jai Shukla - Advocate for the applicant.
 Ms. Shikha Baghel - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/S  ORDER

This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.553/2023 registered at Police Station- Rampur Naikin, District-Sidhi (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 363 r/w 109, 366 and 376(3) of IPC and Section 17 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in custody since 22.06.2023.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the victim on her own volition went with the applicant.
The applicant had not kidnapped or abducted her.

In her statement recorded under Section 183 of BNSS, she has stated that she was knowing the applicant and they were talking each other on telephone, hence, it is clear that she was consenting party and the other two accused persons have been granted the benefit of bail, hence, the applicant is also entitled to be released on bail.
Learned counsel for the State has opposed and has submitted that the victim was minor and the offence was committed.
Looking to the age of the victim, the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
5.

The age of the victim at the time of offence was 15 years and 5 months thus, she was minor, hence,
her consent has no value.
